commented_text: 3.8 System documentation The primary documentation is a maintained project repository with a clear README covering the purpose of the prototype, the required environment, the main pipeline steps, reproduction instructions, and output organization. For a software-based thesis this is the most useful form because it stays close to the code and can be updated as the implementation changes. The report itself documents the system architecture, the data flow from benchmark sample to routing label, the evaluation procedure, and the main configuration choices. Detailed operational material can be placed in an appendix if needed. The guiding standard is traceability. Any reported result should be traceable back to the dataset split, retrieval outputs, judge labels, router predictions, and evaluation procedure that produced it. Since the prototype is an experimental research system rather than a deployed service, this matters more than a separate operations manual.
